pick.headline: US and Britain charge two Libyan intelligence officers over Lockerbie
pick.summary: On 14 November 1991 the United States and Britain announced charges against two Libyans, Abdelbaset al-Megrahi and Lamin Khalifah Fhimah, alleged officers of Libyan intelligence, for the bombing of Pan Am flight 103.
pick.significance: The indictments ended speculation that Iran or Syria had been responsible, and led to UN sanctions on Libya when Tripoli refused to hand the men over.
pick.fbis: Tripoli's JANA carried a statement on 15 November from Libya's People's Bureau for Foreign Liaison denying any Libyan involvement in the Lockerbie bombing.

alternates.headline: Prince Sihanouk returns to Phnom Penh
alternates.summary: On 14 November 1991 Prince Norodom Sihanouk returned to Phnom Penh after nearly thirteen years in exile, under the Paris peace agreements signed the previous month.
alternates.significance: His return was the visible start of the UN-supervised settlement that ended Cambodia's war.
alternates.fbis: Phnom Penh's SPK news agency reported on 14 November that Prince Norodom Sihanouk had left China for Cambodia early that morning.
